text_fidelity_a:
WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black I give this drive five stars for its size - its physical dimensions - because although I have the same quibbles about it as I do with all other external drives, its size is smaller than other 2.5" external hard drives I've seen, including the 1.5TB Seagate that I own.

In the 2.5" hard drive world - the drives that can run on just USB power - there are internal drives that you can pair with an external case and there are external drives that come in a case and with software - usually a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to help the layman back things up. Unlike the 3.5" hard drive world, capacities are larger earlier in the external devices, but somehow the casing and enclosed bridge (in this case SATA to USB) make the physical size larger than an internal drive with case. This one is still a little bigger, but really quite small. It's awesome, frankly. To have that much capacity in something you can store just about anywhere and you don't even have to mess around with a power cord.

What I don't like - and I complain about this with all external hard drives - is the included software that they want you to install to do backups, etc. As an advanced computer user, I think it's nonsense; even my mother should be able to use the drive without any software. Of course you don't have to use it. The thing that annoys me is that the drive - again, like all other externals nowadays - comes with a sleep timer set, in this case at 30 minutes, so I have to install the interface software to turn that off (necessary for my intended application), and then uninstall the software to get it off my system, but all software leaves a trace after its removal.

If this is your first USB 3.0 peripheral, be aware that the port on the drive is unlike any USB 2.0 port, and thus will require a different cable if you need one longer than the included ~1m cable. More industry stupidity, so they can overcharge for the first year or so. Look for a cheap one on Amazon so you don't have to run out to Best Buy and pay 10x too much. Interface cables are the one thing I believe in buying as cheap as possible - and thank God for Amazon in that respect.

One more note in response to another review: prices on non-solid state hard drives have been fluctuating a lot recently because of the Thai floods, and prices of electronics on Amazon always fluctuate. I typically check all prices before buying anything, but still end up buying from Amazon 99% of the time. I haven't seen Best Buy have a real deal in years. They make their money off lies that their employees tell you, either because they have been brainwashed in to believing said lies or because of commission. Do your own price comparison when the time comes to make a purchase.

The only thing I don't love about this drive is an industry problem that's not going away any time soon, and I have to just stop complaining about it (later). I give this a higher than average review because I was actually surprised - and impressed - with the physical size.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black

text_fidelity_a:
Active Noise Cancelling Headphone Built-in Mic Over Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone Foldable Hi-Fi Stereo Headset with Wired Mode for Airplanes Travel TV PC Cell Phones They got just about everything right with these. They're comfortable, simple and elegant design, and with good sound quality. I like that they can work via Bluetooth and with an analogue input because, obviously, you want to be able to use them with the plane's entertainment system. It also comes with an adapter for the split-style analogue inputs that some planes use (to keep you from stealing their headphones).

I haven't used noise cancelling headphones before this, and as I suspected, they don't work miracles, but they do help a lot. It is crazy how voices seem further away, although it will only help so much if you end up between a yappy couple that didn't want to sit directly beside each other for some reason. It does block out a lot of other sounds completely. It is just white noise (if it's more than that, I wouldn't know what), so the effects vary depending on what you are trying to cancel.

Interesting that the music you are listening to sound different depending if you have noise cancelling on or not. They both sound good, but I think it sounds better with noise cancelling on, oddly enough. I listen to loud stuff, but I suspect some people might like to pair the noise cancelling with some kind of light music or bird noises or something to try to sleep on a plane.

Obviously, the inherent drawback is that if you're using these to try to sleep on a plane, you now have something big on your head limiting the positions in which your head can take. But they are about as comfortable as any could possibly be, I think.

Nice case comes with it. They fold up in a crazy way that surprised me slightly the first time. The one thing I identified that should have been better: there is a sort of needless wrist strap on the case that starts where the zipper starts. If they put it on the other side, where the zipper ends, then you could fold it into the case when you don't want it. Of course, you can just cut it off if you don't ever want it.

These are enough to get you dirty looks from the flight attendants for not hearing them when they speak directly to you. Use with some common sense.
text_fidelity_b: Active Noise Cancelling Headphone Built-in Mic Over Ear Wireless Bluetooth Headphone Foldable Hi-Fi Stereo Headset with Wired Mode for Airplanes Travel TV PC Cell Phones

I still have 100’s of CDs though. But, I actually got this for my mom who hasn’t been able to update her CD collection.

As far as me? I definitely won’t need one right now. I definitely wouldn’t get this though.

text_fidelity_a:
JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV) 3.5 stars taking price into account

With headphones, it is always a blend of "you get what you paid for", and comparing to others at a similar price point.
How do these compare? Well, they are about average for the $20-$40 range. Not much better, not much worse. And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.
text_fidelity_b: JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV)

My requirements were portability and ease of use. Since I already owned the best USB hub in the world made by Plugable that lasts for what seems forever, I decided to purchase a new card reader of the same brand. I am very glad that I have made this choice.

My new bright green Plugable multi-card reader arrived shortly and was promptly put to use. It's a well built gadget; the only con is that it has a fairly short cord so it might not be useful in some setups; however it did just fine in mine. The cord is 4 inches long and the USB plug going into the port is about one inch long, so it's best used on the desktop surface. It does require the included external power cord. Rated as a SuperSpeed USB 3.0, it's backwards compatible with 2.0 as well. This card reader supports Micro SD, SD, SDHC, SDXC, MMC, MS, and MSXC card formats; all the corresponding cards slots are clearly marked which eliminates guesswork. Its bright green top makes it easy to be spotted, especially on the darker shade desk surfaces like mine. The card inserts easily and smoothly.

It works wonders; once a card is inserted, it is being read promptly and then formatted quickly, a telltale sign of a great functioning card reader. I keep it plugged in the USB port of the hub at all times. I can wholeheartedly recommend the Plugable multi-card reader; buy it, you won't regret it.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L is USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras I upgraded to this lens from the non-IS version of the 70-200mm as I was having problems getting sharp shots not affected by hand shake. The lens is rather long and heavy and the image stabilization comes in quite handy, especially with shots under low light conditions when you don't want to raise the ISO too high to compensate. The IS can generally get you 2 stops more light than what you might ordinarily expect before experiencing hand shake blur.

Images from this lens are very nice - sharp and good color, good bokeh at the wider apertures so you get nice separation between subject and background. I took this lens to the zoo once and got lots of good shots with it, I've been very pleased with its performance.

I use this lens on a full-frame camera, so keep in mind that if you are buying this for a camera with a cropped sensor, the actual focal range is more like a 110-320mm.

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers For an apartment with only one door and one window that opens this set is great. But most places need a few more. For a dorm room this is fine. I've only seen dorm rooms that had one door and usually the dorm rooms windows are several stories up so it would probably be pretty hard for someone to enter that way. Unless it's on the ground floor.

The door stop alarm is extremely LOUD. And it will not stop SCREAMING until it is physically switched off. This is the first of this type I have ever tried out. A few years ago I bought about 10 door stop alarms of another brand and they were also very loud. However, once the pressure plate was released back up they would stop screaming. I guess it's good that it continues to scream until you stop it. Especially in a dorm type living situation. Someone would eventually come to see what was the matter. It takes one 9 volt battery.

The window alarm is extremely simple to install and the double sided sticky tape that comes with it is very strong. I have several of these window alarms attached to various windows at my home. They aren't the loudest but they should get the job done of scaring off an unwanted intruder. It takes 4 LR44 button batteries.

The personal key chain alarm is o.k. It's got a loud scream that makes my ears ring. It takes a good tug to pull out the pin to activate it. The small LED light is better than no light at all but don't expect a bright beam. It will help you find your keys if you dropped them in the dark. I think along with a sincere scream for help and the personal alarm screaming as well, I would think most aggressors would give up and try for an easier target.......at least I would hope so. It takes 3 LR44 button batteries.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed I have had this unit for about four years now. Never a problem. I use it for storing media files and my digital Paintings. It was used for four years on a MacPro 3,1, connected via USB 2. Upgraded the drives over the years, so now it has two 4TB and two 2TB Seagate HDDs.
I just purchased a new (to me) MacPro Trash Can, so I will try the USB 3.
This enclosure is heavy, and not bad looking. The plastic faceplate comes off easy (as it was probably designed to do, to allow easy changing the Hard Drives). But again chances are once you get the drives installed and settings just so, you will not be messing with the door/faceplate. it has tow plastic pins on the bottom and a "latch (Spring loaded)" press and it pops off or on.
The power cord goes in the side, which is weird but not a deal breaker. And unusual configuration, but it is pretty solid and really I don't really mess with it very oftern).
Three fan settings and yes two of them are not quiet. I leave mine on auto and unless I am working on a hot day, moving or writing tons of files, don't hear the fan at all).
The LED lights are not an issue for me, but I could see where in a dark room it would bother some folks. (electrical tape if it really errkks you).
Getting the settings the way you want them takes some trial and error, but once you have them you will most likely not mess with them again.
Drives are easy to add or remove, a couple screws, slide it in the slot.
I have found that if the drive has been formatted and contains data when you add it, you have to force mount it, but once that is done no issues.
So if possible initialize the drive in the enclosure.
This is ideal for novice of mid-level tech geeks, or folks who have a large media collection (Music, movies, photos, etc).
I have hooked it up directly to my Mac Pro and my Wireless router (Orbi) so anyone authorized to access the network can access the media files on it. So my Photos on one drive, Movies on two drives and music on the last drive.
I would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to create a media server.
It DOES NOT have RAID built-in, it can be added via software, but, for a few bucks more you can get the RAID version of this.
text_fidelity_b: Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed

text_fidelity_a: TRENDnet 300 Mbps Wireless Easy-N-Upgrader (TEW-637AP) First let me say I have set up a domain and load balancer that both work flawlessly. Having said that, this thing is junk. I must have received a dud. I did not use the CD. Its default IP is 192.168.10.100. So in order to access it I had to change my subnet and IP to 192.168.10.99 on my laptop. After that was done I logged on and set it up. Really strait forward no surprises here. Five mins in and my wireless network kept dropping at random. Very very very annoying. I downloaded the newest drivers from their website and it fixed nothing. I wrote tech support and they told me I needed to update with Internet Explorer 6. WTF, IE6 came out in like 2006. I am running windows 7, how in the world am I suppose to install IE6. Regardless of all that, why would me installing the firmware on IE6 change anything. The router has checksum routines I am it uses before flashing its memory. This really makes no sense what-so-ever! Anyway after 2 days of messing with it I sent it back and just setup a linksys router with the WRT mod and everything is great now. Honestly I feel like these positive reviews are all fake.

Osprey Apogee Men's Laptop Backpack , Kraken Blue This is a lot of pack in a what amounts to a small package. I own about 4 Ospray packs, and use them for things varying from a city man bag, to hiking day bag, backpacking bag, and this. This is actually 4 litres larger than my ospray day pack, but feels much smaller and more compact.

The main features are:

Padded laptop and separate zippered tablet sleeve (fits up to a 15” laptop)
--This is a great and mirrors what you will see in may backpacks/laptop packs. It includes a padded sleeve but also magazine sleeves. Good for keeping things like travel documents and reading material separate from your laptop

Front panel organization pocket with key clip
--This is a large pocket, and goes all the way down to the bottom of the pack. it has three pockets across the top of the pouch and good for various things, but for a business bag, doesn't have a small zippered pouch, nor does it have a small pockets for pens/pencils. Wish it had that.

Hidden side access dual stretch mesh water bottle pockets
--Took me a few days to find these, these are well hidden and grant you access to you water bottle from the back area of the pack, instead of feeding right from the top. The stretch mesh fits most standard camelbak type water bottles and holds them excellently. I've lost bottles before, this will hold them like a miser holding on to his last penny.

Heat embossed scratch-free slash pocket and blinker light attachment point
--Good for things that may scratch, like a pair of glasses, your phone, etc.

The whole bag is wonderfully made. Typical of an Ospray bag. Very sturdy with good stitching and with well placed and useful lashing straps. The bag has typical sholder straps that connect across the chest with a whistle and there is also a waist strap.

Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All This is one of those products that is good to have, but even better if you never need to use it since you'll probably be using it when the electricity is out. It offers a lot of functionality in a compact size: a flashlight, AM radio, FM radio and weather band radio. It runs off of an internal rechargeable battery that is kept charged either via solar power, USB connection or by cranking the handle. It can also serve as a source to charge a cell phone (albeit with very limited capacity to do so since the internal battery is only rated at 800mAh).

It works pretty well. The flashlight is very bright - had no problems lighting my way down a dark stairway and in a totally dark room. The radio is OK. The reception is spotty and it only picked up a few of the very strong stations in the area. It's very susceptible to positioning - moving it just a couple of inches turned a clear station into static.

Cranking the handle to keep it charged is pretty easy. It turns easily and the handle is comfortable. According to the manual, one minute of cranking equals 30 minutes of flashlight use or 20 minutes of radio use.

This is a good product to keep on hand in case of emergency, such as a bad storm or extended power outage. It won't keep you cool in the summer or warm in the winter, but at least you can see where you're going and listen to the radio. Definitely worth a spot in the emergency kit. The only shortcoming is the somewhat limited radio reception.
[sample provided by manufacturer for review]
text_fidelity_b: Epica Digital Emergency Solar Hand Crank AM/FM/NOAA Radio, Flashlight, Smartphone Charger with NOAA Certified Weather Alert & Cable-ONE Cable Does All

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) [[VIDEOID:c23012732deceb9d78b96d41ac89bfcb]] [[VIDEOID:56e6589f81a80deb1709b51fc87a42ef]] [[VIDEOID:bdf9b77251e219b84bed6372225dbf2a]] [[VIDEOID:838bfc2c03ad2a6d884b05f4a37eddbe]] [[VIDEOID:f7f3bb80516774e2cc828f076249211a]] [[VIDEOID:d48cd1a96b9a119e675001d320845a53]] [[VIDEOID:9363c8a20797fe64545aeb51179ca502]] [[VIDEOID:3371609d21e77efbab0cfd0f6265a782]] This is a terrific little action camera that has remarkable clear video, good audio and is extremely easy to use. I understand there were some problems with audio in the earlier versions, but it seems to be all fixed now because the sound quality was excellent when tested both indoors and outside.

I won't bore you with going over all of the specs which you can read in the product description, but I'll tell you how easy it is to use. Mine arrived partially charged, so I used my fingernail to open the back port and inset the included 8gb micro SD card, then charged it fully within an hour. On a full battery it can operate for about 107 minutes and when depleted it takes between 1.5 to 2 hrs to fully charge.

I downloaded the app to my iPad for free from the app store, then did some testing. It connected easily to my WiFi and the interface understandable and easy to use giving you the choice to shoot still photos or videos in several different resolutions. You can also import the photos or videos taken with the camera to your cell phone, your iPad, or share them using the WiFi connection to import them.

This little camera takes gorgeous high def photos, and the audio inside is crystal clear. When I was offered the opportunity by the manufacturer to test the Cube+ I went ahead and purchased a [[ASIN:B00NXK3JTI Polaroid Helmet Mount for the Polaroid CUBE, CUBE+ HD Action Lifestyle Camera]] so I would be able to properly test it in action in order to determine video and sound quality outside in the elements.

I attached the helmet mount to my 9 y/o granddaughter's helmet, placed the Cube+ in it, started it through the app on my iPad and sent her out on her scooter to see how the video and audio quality was. I've attached a short part of the video here so you can assess it for yourself, but I'm quite pleased with the quality of both the picture and the sound, and I didn't experience any lag time in regards to the app.

It does record video in MP4 format, so if you have trouble hearing the audio on your computer you should download QuickTime Player or VLC Player. Both downloads are free and should allow you to view the files and hear the audio. VLC also has a free converter available in case you prefer to use Windows Media Player or Windows Movie Maker. I use a free app called Trim & Cut on my iPad which shortens, condenses, and converts my videos to the format I prefer, and that's what I used for the video I've attached here.

This is a reasonably priced tough little action camera that's easy to use and produces great quality video. It's weather resistant and splashproof so it can handle the outdoors already, but I plan to buy the waterproof case for it so we can have fun swimming with it on this summer. I don't own a GoPro, so I have nothing to compare this to, but from a user's stand point I can definitely tell you that this is user friendly, easy to operate and does a remarkably good job! Enjoy!

This camera was provided at no cost by the manufacturer for evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
Sabrent 4 Port Portable USB 3.0 Hub for Ultra Book, MacBook Air, Windows 8 Tablet PC - Black (HB-RU34) This is a great choice if you need a USB hub but don’t have much room. It’s only 1.25 inches wide and 4.75 inches long. Very slim profile that makes it easy to fit onto a desk or next to a laptop.

The 4 USB 3.0 output ports are arranged along the top; the input port is on the end. As shipped, this is a passive port (e.g., no external power) but it does have a power input at the end for a DC 5V input. The power transformer needed is NOT included in the package. The only attachment included is a USB input cord.

There is an indicator LED to show it is receiving power. I didn’t have any problems using it with USB 3.0 and 2.0 devices. However, since it’s a passive hub, it’s not the best choice for really power-hungry devices, such as large external drives or for tasks such as charging a tablet. Those applications are better suited to a hub with an external power source.

The build quality seems very good. It’s plastic, but the case feels pretty durable. The ports are well-anchored and didn’t move when I stressed the input cables.

It’s well worth considering if you need a slim profile passive hub for USB 3.0 devices.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sabrent 4 Port Portable USB 3.0 Hub for Ultra Book, MacBook Air, Windows 8 Tablet PC - Black (HB-RU34)

Also, the remote does not automatically pair with your phone the next time you want to use it, so you have to pair them over again. This is a bit annoying.

I have a Note 10+ with a case and it barely fits into the holder. I'm so glad it does. The whole setup feels nice and sturdy all the way around, from the bottom of the stand to phone holders. I sell bulk bought makeup online, and it's nice to have a ring big enough that it doesn't show up on the surface of the shiny palettes. I can place it so there are no shadows or bright spots, and the light is up far enough that it is not in my way. It is that big. I am working with four to six inch items, so that helps, too. It makes my life so much easier.

The ten inch ring light is great for getting perfect shoe photos. I love buying shoes, and always take photos to put on the end of the boxes, so I can see exactly what I have at a glance. It makes picking out my shoes for the day easy, when I can see the actual shoe, and not a drawing of it.

These lights are the best I've bought. They are made very well, and so is everything they come with. You will not find a better setup at a better cost. A beginner or novice will have everything you need to start taking photos or videos right out of the box. You may, however, find better instructions on how to put a setup together in a different set, but then you wouldn't get half the amount or half the quality of the items you get in this one. It may take some trial and error, but if I can figure out how to set this up, I'm pretty sure anyone can. I have cognitive difficulties and things don't come easy. It took me a good while and I did ask for some help with one thing from my son, but I got it done, and it was worth the trouble. 4 stars ✨
